tool.name: Panagram index
tool.description: : an alignment-free pan-k-mer index of genome assemblies
tool.command: ## Galaxy flattens newlines in <command>, so the work is a shell script; its inputs are argv. bash '$script' '$samples' '$k' '$anchors' '$advanced.max_bin_kbp' '$advanced.lowres_step' '$advanced.min_bin_count' '$advanced.gff_gene_types' '$index.extra_files_path' '$genome_dist' '$logs' '$keep_bitvectors' #if $keep_bitvectors '$bitvectors' #else none #end if

configfiles.configfile: #import re name fasta gff id anchor #set $gff_by_name = {} #if $gffs #for $g in $gffs #silent $gff_by_name.update({re.sub(r'\.gff3?$', '', str($g.element_identifier)): str($g)}) #end for #end if #set $anchor_set = [a for a in re.split(r'[\s,]+', str($anchors)) if a] #for $i, $f in enumerate($genomes) #set $name = re.sub(r'\.(fa|fasta|fna|fas)$', '', str($f.element_identifier)) ${name} ${f} ${gff_by_name.get($name, '')} ${i} ${'True' if $name in $anchor_set else 'False'} #end for

set -eu samples="\$1"; k="\$2"; anchors="\$3"; max_bin_kbp="\$4"; lowres_step="\$5"; min_bin_count="\$6" gene_types="\$7"; index_dir="\$8"; genome_dist="\$9"; logs="\${10}"; keep_bitvectors="\${11}"; bitvectors="\${12}" \#\# Names are written verbatim into a kmc_tools script whose tokenizer reads '-' as subtraction, so only \#\# letters, digits and _ are accepted; a name that would break the build is refused before KMC runs. names=`awk -F '	' 'NR > 1 { print \$1 }' "\$samples"` for n in \$names; do case "\$n" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_]*) echo "genome name must be letters, digits or _: '\$n' (from its element identifier)" >&2; exit 1;; esac done dups=`printf '%s
' \$names | sort | uniq -d` [ -z "\$dups" ] || { echo "genome name given twice: \$dups" >&2; exit 1; } anchor_list=`echo "\$anchors" | tr ',' ' '` anchor_list=`echo \$anchor_list` [ -n "`echo \$anchor_list`" ] || { echo "no anchor genome given" >&2; exit 1; } for a in \$anchor_list; do printf '%s
' \$names | grep -qx "\$a" || { echo "anchor \$a is not one of the genomes" >&2; exit 1; } done \#\# A GFF3 whose name matches no genome would be silently ignored, so it is refused. awk -F '	' 'NR > 1 && \$3 != "" { n++ } END { print n + 0 }' "\$samples" > gff_count echo "genomes: `printf '%s
' \$names | wc -l | tr -d ' '`; anchors: \$anchor_list; annotated: `cat gff_count`" slots="\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" mem_mb="\${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-8192}" kmc_gb=`expr \$mem_mb / 1024 / \$slots` [ "\$kmc_gb" -ge 1 ] || kmc_gb=1 mkdir -p index/tmp cp "\$samples" index/samples.tsv cd index export TMPDIR="\$PWD/tmp" panagram index samples.tsv -k "\$k" -c "\$slots" --anchor_genomes \$anchor_list --max_bin_kbp "\$max_bin_kbp" --lowres_step "\$lowres_step" --min_bin_count "\$min_bin_count" --gff_gene_types \$gene_types --kmc.memory "\$kmc_gb" --kmc.threads "\$slots" --prepare \#\# Snakemake 9 reads a target placed right after --resources' values as a resource, so it comes first. snakemake all --cores "\$slots" --resources mem_mb="\$mem_mb" > ../snakemake.log 2>&1 || { tail -n 50 ../snakemake.log >&2; exit 1; } tail -n 3 ../snakemake.log cp ../snakemake.log logs/snakemake.log \#\# The viewable index: what `panagram view` reads, without KMC's databases or temporary files. mkdir -p "\$index_dir" cp -R config.yaml samples.tsv genome_dist.tsv anchor "\$index_dir"/ cp genome_dist.tsv "\$genome_dist" tar -cf "\$logs" logs \#\# The bitvector databases are all a later anchor needs from kmc/ (with the FASTAs and any GFF3). if [ "\$keep_bitvectors" = "true" ]; then tar -cf "\$bitvectors" kmc/bitvec*.kmc_* kmc/opdef*.txt fi

param.name: genomes
param.label: Genome assemblies
param.help: A list of FASTAs, one per genome. The list's order is part of the index (each genome's bit is its position). A genome's name is its element identifier, less a FASTA extension; letters, digits and _ only.

param.name: anchors
param.label: Anchor genomes
param.help: Names of the genomes to index in their own coordinates, separated by commas or spaces. Each anchor costs one indexing job and its own index.

validator.message: Genome names separated by commas or spaces

param.name: gffs
param.label: Gene annotations for anchors
param.help: GFF3 files named like the genome they annotate (refA.gff3 for refA). Read only for anchors.

param.name: keep_bitvectors
param.label: Also output the bitvector databases
param.help: KMC's merged bitvectors and their opdef files, which is all a later anchor needs from the KMC step (with the same FASTAs).

param.label: GFF3 feature types indexed as genes

has_text.text: anchor hapX is not one of the genomes
genome name must be letters, digits or _: 'ref-A'

tool.help:
**What it does**
Builds a Panagram_ index: the k-mers of every genome are counted with KMC, and each *anchor* genome is annotated, position by position, with which genomes share the k-mer that starts there. The index shows the presence and absence of sequence across genomes without aligning them.
The tool runs ``panagram index --prepare`` and then the Snakemake workflow it writes, with ``--cores`` from the job's slots and ``--resources mem_mb`` from its memory.
**Inputs**
- *Genome assemblies*: a list of FASTAs, one per genome. The list's order is part of the index (a genome's bit is its position). A genome's name is its element identifier less ``.fa``, ``.fasta``, ``.fna`` or ``.fas``; names are letters, digits and ``_`` only, because Panagram passes them to ``kmc_tools``, which reads ``-`` as subtraction. - *Anchor genomes*: every anchor gets its own bitmap, bins and gene index. Few anchors keep the index small and the run short; anchors must be chromosome-scale, since the browser and every bin are in anchor coordinates. - *Gene annotations*: optional GFF3 files, matched to genomes by name and read for anchors only.
**Outputs**
- *index* (``panagram_index``): ``config.yaml``, ``samples.tsv``, ``genome_dist.tsv`` and ``anchor/``, the directory ``panagram view`` reads. ``anchor/<name>/bitsum.bins.tsv`` holds, per bin, the number of positions shared by 0..n genomes. - *genome distances*: Mash distances for every pair of genomes (``genome_dist.tsv``: genome, genome, distance, p-value, shared hashes). - *logs*: Panagram's and Snakemake's logs, with per-step benchmarks. - *bitvector databases* (optional): ``kmc/bitvec*`` and ``kmc/opdef*.txt``, which a later anchor needs; the per-genome KMC databases are not kept.
.. warning:: KMC's databases are large: about 4 bytes per input base were kept in a cannabis test, so the job needs several times the total input size in free disk.
The genome and chromosome UMAP coordinates in the index are not reproducible between runs, even with the same inputs; the bitmaps, bins and distances are.
.. _Panagram: https://github.com/kjenike/panagram
